q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-17#ex: Prussian soldiers fired into the crowd, killing eleven people. Heinrich Heine wrote the poem The Silesian Weavers about it, and Gerhart Hauptmann the play The Weavers in 1892.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-18#qu: What caused the Great Famine in Ireland from 1845?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-18#ch: A fungal disease that destroyed the potato harvests
A volcanic eruption that caused summers to fail
An epidemic that killed the livestock
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-18#ex: The poor rural population lived almost entirely on potatoes. About one million people died and millions emigrated to North America, while grain continued to be exported to England.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-19#qu: What is the title of Karl Marx's main work, in which he analyzed the capitalist economy?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-19#ch: The Condition of the Working Class in England
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-19#ex: The first volume appeared in 1867. The Condition of the Working Class in England, by contrast, was written by his friend and comrade Friedrich Engels.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-20#qu: With which call does the Communist Manifesto end?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-20#ex: In it Marx and Engels interpreted history as a sequence of class struggles. The text appeared in London in February 1848, shortly before the European revolutions broke out.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-21#qu: In which city did Karl Marx live from 1849 until his death?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-21#ex: Born in Trier, he had been expelled from Germany, France and Belgium as a journalist and revolutionary. His main work, Capital, was written in exile.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-22#qu: What grand project did the British colonial politician Cecil Rhodes dream of?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-22#ch: A railway from Berlin to Baghdad
A British railway from the Cape to Cairo
A canal across the Isthmus of Panama
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-22#ex: Rhodes had built a diamond monopoly with De Beers; his British South Africa Company conquered the territory of present-day Zimbabwe and Zambia, which was named Rhodesia after him.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-23#qu: In which speech did Abraham Lincoln describe democracy as government of the people, by the people, for the people?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-23#ex: Lincoln gave the short address in 1863 at the dedication of the soldiers' cemetery on the Gettysburg battlefield, in the middle of the Civil War.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-24#qu: Which amendment to the US Constitution abolished slavery in 1865?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-24#ex: Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation of 1863 had only declared the enslaved in the rebellious Southern states free. The 13th Amendment ended slavery throughout the United States.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-25#qu: Against which states did Prussia fight the three wars of unification that led to the founding of the German Empire in 1871?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-25#ex: Prussia fought Denmark in 1864, Austria in 1866 and France in 1870–71. Italy was in fact Prussia's ally in 1866.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-26#qu: Where was Wilhelm I proclaimed German Emperor on January 18, 1871?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-26#ch: In St. Paul's Church in Frankfurt
In the City Palace in Berlin
In the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-26#ex: The proclamation in the palace of the defeated enemy humiliated France. In 1919 the peace treaty ending the First World War was signed in the same hall.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-27#qu: Which emperor dismissed Chancellor Otto von Bismarck in 1890?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-27#ex: The young emperor, who had come to the throne in 1888, the Year of the Three Emperors, wanted to rule himself and parted ways with the old chancellor after disputes.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-28#qu: Under Prussia's three-class franchise, what determined the weight of a vote?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-28#ex: The few highest taxpayers chose as many electors as the great mass of the poorest. For the Reichstag, by contrast, universal male suffrage applied.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-29#qu: Who are regarded as the leading figures in the unification of Italy between 1859 and 1870?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-29#ex: Piedmont's prime minister Cavour pursued unification through diplomacy, while the guerrilla leader Garibaldi conquered Sicily and Naples with his Expedition of the Thousand in 1860. The Kingdom of Italy was founded in 1861.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-30#qu: Which seas does the Suez Canal, opened in 1869, connect?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-30#ch: The Mediterranean and the Black Sea
The Red Sea and the Persian Gulf
The Mediterranean and the Red Sea
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-30#ex: Ships traveling from Europe to India no longer had to sail around Africa. In 1882 Britain occupied Egypt to secure the canal.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-31#qu: Which European great power did Japan defeat in the war of 1904–05?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-31#ex: It was the first time an Asian power had beaten a European great power. Since the Meiji Restoration, Japan had rapidly become an industrial and military power.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-32#qu: Which country used warships to force Japan to open up in 1853?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-32#ex: Commodore Matthew Perry appeared in Edo Bay with his "black ships". The forced opening contributed to the fall of the shogunate in 1868.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-33#qu: Against whom was the Boxer Rebellion in China around 1900 directed?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-33#ch: Against the large landowners in the south
Against foreigners, missionaries and Chinese Christians
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-33#ex: In 1900 the Boxers besieged the Legation Quarter in Beijing, at times with the support of the imperial court. An expeditionary force from eight nations crushed the uprising, and China had to pay enormous reparations.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-34#qu: Which two African states were not under European colonial rule around 1914?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-34#ex: Ethiopia repelled an Italian army at Adwa in 1896. Liberia had been founded by freed slaves from the United States.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-35#qu: Which general drove the Herero into the Omaheke desert after the Battle of Waterberg in 1904?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-35#ex: Von Trotha ordered that every Herero be shot; up to 80 percent of the Herero and half of the Nama died. In 2021 the Federal Republic of Germany recognized the crimes as genocide.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-36#qu: Which invention did Thomas Edison make practical for everyday use in 1879?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-36#ex: In 1882 Edison opened the Pearl Street Station in New York, the first central power station in the United States. In his laboratory at Menlo Park, teams of mechanics and scientists systematically developed new inventions.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-37#qu: Who developed the dynamo in 1866, making it possible to generate electricity in large quantities?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-37#ex: Siemens used the dynamo-electric principle. With electricity, the second Industrial Revolution began from around 1870.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-38#qu: Who achieved the first controlled powered flight at Kitty Hawk in 1903?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-38#ex: On December 17, 1903 Orville Wright stayed in the air for twelve seconds. The two bicycle mechanics had experimented with gliders for years beforehand.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-39#qu: What pioneering feat did Bertha Benz accomplish in August 1888?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-39#ch: The first powered flight by a woman
The first long-distance journey by automobile
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-39#ex: Without her husband's knowledge she drove with her sons from Mannheim to Pforzheim, proving that Carl Benz's motor car was fit for everyday use.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-40#qu: Which element, discovered in 1898, did Marie Curie name after her home country?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-40#ex: Born in Warsaw, she discovered polonium and radium together with her husband Pierre. She remains the only person to have won Nobel Prizes in two natural sciences.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-41#qu: In which war did Florence Nightingale lay the foundations of modern nursing through hygiene from 1854?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-41#ex: In the military hospital at Scutari more soldiers died of disease than of wounds. With cleanliness, fresh linen and better food she drastically reduced the death rate.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-42#qu: What were the militant women's rights activists around Emmeline Pankhurst called?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-42#ex: Their Women's Social and Political Union, founded in 1903, resorted to disruptive actions and hunger strikes. In 1918 British women over 30 won the vote.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-43#qu: For what occasion was the Eiffel Tower built in Paris in 1889?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-43#ex: The world's fairs from London 1851 to Paris 1900 staged technology and colonies as a spectacle for millions of visitors. At the time the tower was the tallest structure in the world.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-44#qu: Which painter belonged to the Impressionists, who painted railway stations, boulevards and the light of the big city?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-44#ex: The movement takes its name from Monet's painting Impression, Sunrise. Among other subjects, he painted the Gare Saint-Lazare in Paris several times.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-45#qu: Which pathogen did Robert Koch discover in 1882?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-45#ex: Tuberculosis was then one of the most common causes of death; Koch received the Nobel Prize for this work in 1905. Alongside Louis Pasteur he is regarded as a founder of bacteriology.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-46#qu: What is the German name for the stock market crash of 1873 that followed the boom after the founding of the Empire?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-46#ex: French reparations and speculation had set off a wave of company start-ups. The collapse ushered in a long period of weak growth.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-47#qu: What did the Bessemer process of 1856 make possible?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-47#ch: The extraction of gasoline from crude oil
The cheap production of steel in large quantities
The generation of electricity from water power
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-47#ex: In the process, air is blown through molten pig iron. Cheap steel became indispensable for rails, bridges, ships and skyscrapers.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-48#qu: What did the British Factory Act of 1833 regulate?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-48#ch: It gave factory workers the vote
It restricted child labor in textile mills
It abolished slavery in the colonies
It permitted the founding of trade unions
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-48#ex: It banned the employment of children under nine in textile mills, limited the working hours of older children and introduced state factory inspectors for the first time.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-49#qu: Which country separated church and state by law in 1905?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-49#ex: The law guaranteed freedom of religion but ended state payment of the clergy. The principle of laïcité still shapes France today.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-50#qu: Which company brought the painkiller aspirin onto the market in 1899?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-50#ex: Around 1900 the German chemical industry led the world, developing synthetic dyes and fertilizers as well as medicines.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-51#qu: Which states concluded the Dual Alliance of 1879?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-51#ex: The alliance lasted until 1918. From 1904 it was opposed by the Entente Cordiale between Great Britain and France.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-52#qu: What is meant by Social Darwinism?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-52#ch: Applying natural selection to societies and peoples
A movement for better working conditions in factories
The doctrine of the equality of all people
A church movement opposing Darwin's theory
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-52#ex: Social Darwinists claimed that stronger peoples prevailed in the struggle for existence, and used this to justify racism and imperialism – a misuse of Darwin's biology.
q-islamische-welt-01#question: Which event marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar?
q-islamische-welt-01#explanation: Muhammad's emigration from Mecca to Medina in the year 622 was fixed by Caliph Umar as the beginning of the Islamic calendar.
q-islamische-welt-02#question: Who defeated an Arab-Berber army at Tours and Poitiers in 732?
q-islamische-welt-02#explanation: In 732 the Frankish mayor of the palace Charles Martel halted the advance of Muslim troops to the north.
q-islamische-welt-03#question: Which dynasty founded the city of Baghdad in 762?
q-islamische-welt-03#explanation: In 762 the Abbasid caliph al-Mansur had the round city of Baghdad built on the Tigris as his new capital.
q-islamische-welt-04#question: Which work made Ibn Sina (Avicenna) famous in Europe into the 17th century?
q-islamische-welt-04#explanation: In Latin translation, Ibn Sina's Canon of Medicine was for centuries the most important medical textbook at European universities.
q-islamische-welt-05#question: In which year did Saladin recapture Jerusalem from the Crusaders?
q-islamische-welt-05#explanation: After his victory at Hattin, Saladin took Jerusalem on October 2, 1187; the conquest by the First Crusade had taken place in 1099.
q-islamische-welt-06#question: Who destroyed Baghdad in 1258 and ended the caliphate of the Abbasids?
q-islamische-welt-06#explanation: The Mongol army of Hulagu, a grandson of Genghis Khan, captured Baghdad in 1258 and had the last Abbasid caliph executed.
q-islamische-welt-07#question: Which event of 680 remains of central importance for Shiites to this day?
q-islamische-welt-07#choices.1: The death of Husayn at Karbala
q-islamische-welt-07#explanation: Husayn, the grandson of the Prophet, was killed at Karbala in 680 by troops of the Umayyad caliph Yazid; Shiites commemorate his death each year on the Day of Ashura.
q-islamische-welt-08#question: Where does the word algebra come from?
q-islamische-welt-08#choices.0: From the name of the city of Baghdad
q-islamische-welt-08#choices.2: From the name of the mathematician al-Khwarizmi
q-islamische-welt-08#choices.3: From the title of a book of calculation by al-Khwarizmi
q-islamische-welt-08#explanation: Al-Khwarizmi's book on calculating by completion and balancing, in Arabic al-jabr, gave algebra its name; his own name, by contrast, gave rise to the word algorithm.
q-islamische-welt-09#question: Which dynasty founded the city of Cairo in 969?
q-islamische-welt-09#explanation: The Shiite Fatimids conquered Egypt in 969 and laid out the palace city of al-Qahira, which became Cairo; construction of the al-Azhar mosque began in 970.
q-islamische-welt-10#question: What was the consequence of the Battle of Manzikert in 1071?
q-islamische-welt-10#explanation: After the Seljuk victory over Byzantium, Turkic tribes settled Asia Minor, where the Sultanate of Rum and later the Ottoman Empire arose.
q-islamische-welt-11#question: Who endowed the al-Qarawiyyin mosque in Fez in 859, from which one of the oldest universities in the world developed?
q-islamische-welt-11#explanation: Fatima al-Fihri, the daughter of a merchant, financed the building of the mosque out of her inheritance; the University of al-Qarawiyyin still exists today.
q-islamische-welt-12#question: What happened in Granada on January 2, 1492?
q-islamische-welt-12#choices.3: The last emir handed the city over to the Catholic Monarchs
q-islamische-welt-12#explanation: With the surrender of Granada by Muhammad XII, known as Boabdil, to Isabella and Ferdinand, Muslim rule in Spain ended after almost 800 years.
q-islamische-welt-13#question: Where, according to Islamic tradition, did Muhammad receive his first revelation around 610?
q-islamische-welt-13#choices.3: In a cave on Mount Hira near Mecca
q-islamische-welt-13#explanation: Muhammad withdrew to meditate in the cave on Mount Hira, where according to tradition the angel Gabriel appeared to him. The revelations continued until his death in 632.
q-islamische-welt-14#question: Which woman, as a wife of the Prophet, passed on hundreds of his sayings and taught in Medina?
q-islamische-welt-14#explanation: Aisha, daughter of the first caliph Abu Bakr, is regarded as one of the most important sources for Muhammad's life. After his death she taught in Medina for decades.
q-islamische-welt-15#question: Whom do Shiites regard as Muhammad's rightful successor?
q-islamische-welt-15#choices.0: Ali, the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law
q-islamische-welt-15#explanation: For Shiites, leadership of the community belongs to Ali and his descendants. The name comes from Shiat Ali, the "party of Ali".
q-islamische-welt-16#question: What does the title caliph mean?
q-islamische-welt-16#choices.3: Successor of the Prophet as head of the community
q-islamische-welt-16#explanation: The caliph led the Muslim community with both religious and worldly authority. The first four caliphs were chosen; afterwards the Umayyads and Abbasids made the office hereditary.
q-islamische-welt-17#question: Which caliph took Jerusalem in 638 and guaranteed protection to Christians and Jews?
q-islamische-welt-17#explanation: After the victory over the Byzantines, Jerusalem surrendered to the second caliph, Umar. Abu Bakr had already died in 634.
q-islamische-welt-18#question: Under which caliph was the Quran written down in a binding, uniform version around 650?
q-islamische-welt-18#explanation: The third caliph, Uthman, had a uniform version of the Quran produced and divergent copies destroyed. This text remains authoritative today.
q-islamische-welt-19#question: Which city did the Umayyads make the capital of their empire from 661?
q-islamische-welt-19#explanation: Muawiya, the first Umayyad caliph, ruled from Damascus. The city's Umayyad Mosque is one of the oldest surviving great mosques.
q-islamische-welt-20#question: Which region did Arab-Berber troops largely conquer from 711 onward?
q-islamische-welt-20#explanation: In 711 troops under Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed at Gibraltar and within a few years conquered almost all of Spain and Portugal. This became al-Andalus.
q-islamische-welt-21#question: Why did the great Arab siege of Constantinople in 717–718 fail?
q-islamische-welt-21#choices.0: Because an earthquake destroyed the Arab camp
q-islamische-welt-21#choices.1: Because of a Byzantine alliance with the Mongols
q-islamische-welt-21#choices.2: Because of a Frankish relief army under Charles Martel
q-islamische-welt-21#choices.3: Because of the walls, Greek fire and a harsh winter
q-islamische-welt-21#explanation: The mighty land walls, Greek fire against the fleet and a severe winter wore down the besiegers. The Arabs never again attempted such a large attack on the city.
q-islamische-welt-22#question: What were Christians and Jews called who, under Muslim rule, could keep their religion in return for a poll tax?
q-islamische-welt-22#explanation: As dhimmi (protected people) they ran their own communities but paid the jizya poll tax. High offices were usually closed to them.
q-islamische-welt-23#question: From which region did the revolt that overthrew the Umayyads in 750 emerge?
q-islamische-welt-23#explanation: The Abbasid Revolution began in Khorasan in north-eastern Persia. Accordingly, the centre of the empire shifted east to Iraq.
q-islamische-welt-24#question: Where did a surviving Umayyad prince flee after 750 to found his own emirate?
q-islamische-welt-24#explanation: Abd al-Rahman I escaped the Abbasid massacre and founded the Emirate of Córdoba in 756. His descendant Abd al-Rahman III raised it to a caliphate in 929.
q-islamische-welt-25#question: Which Abbasid caliph lives on as a character in the tales of the Thousand and One Nights?
q-islamische-welt-25#explanation: Under Harun al-Rashid (786–809) Baghdad reached its splendour. The Thousand and One Nights turned him into a legendary ruler.
q-islamische-welt-26#question: What was the main task of the House of Wisdom in Baghdad?
q-islamische-welt-26#choices.0: Training military slaves for the army
q-islamische-welt-26#choices.1: Translating Greek, Persian and Indian works into Arabic
q-islamische-welt-26#explanation: Under Caliph al-Mamun the House of Wisdom became the centre of the translation movement. Works by Aristotle, Euclid and Galen were thus preserved and developed further.
q-islamische-welt-27#question: Which achievement did Muslims adopt from India and pass on to Europe?
q-islamische-welt-27#explanation: The Indian numerals including zero became known through Arabic arithmetic books and are therefore called Arabic numerals in Europe. The word cipher goes back to Arabic sifr, "empty, zero".
q-islamische-welt-28#question: From whom did Muslims learn the art of papermaking in the 8th century?
q-islamische-welt-28#explanation: The technique reached Samarkand from China, where the first paper mills of the Islamic world arose, soon followed by Baghdad. Paper made libraries, administration and a lively book trade possible.
q-islamische-welt-29#question: Which modern technical term derives from the name of the mathematician al-Khwarizmi?
q-islamische-welt-29#explanation: The Latin form of his name, Algorismi, gave rise to the term algorithm for a step-by-step calculation procedure. The word algebra, by contrast, comes from the title of his arithmetic book.
q-islamische-welt-30#question: Which field did Ibn al-Haytham refound through experiments?
q-islamische-welt-30#explanation: Ibn al-Haytham explained vision by light travelling from objects into the eye and tested his ideas with experiments. His Book of Optics was translated into Latin and influenced European science.
q-islamische-welt-31#question: What did the scholar al-Biruni calculate with remarkable accuracy in the 11th century?
q-islamische-welt-31#explanation: Al-Biruni determined the Earth's radius with a method using a mountain and the horizon. He also wrote a major work on India and its culture.
q-islamische-welt-32#question: The works of which ancient philosopher did Ibn Rushd mainly study?
q-islamische-welt-32#explanation: Ibn Rushd, known in the West as Averroes, wrote extensive commentaries on Aristotle in Córdoba. In Europe he was therefore simply called "the Commentator".
q-islamische-welt-33#question: What did Ibn Khaldun examine in his Muqaddimah?
q-islamische-welt-33#choices.2: The rise and fall of empires
q-islamische-welt-33#explanation: In the 14th century Ibn Khaldun explained the cycle of dynasties through group cohesion. His work is regarded as one of the beginnings of the social sciences.
q-islamische-welt-34#choices.1: An architectural style with domes and minarets
q-islamische-welt-34#choices.3: One of the four Sunni schools of law
q-islamische-welt-34#explanation: Sufis sought a direct, loving experience of God through prayer, song and asceticism. Their brotherhoods carried Islam to India, Anatolia and Africa.
q-islamische-welt-35#question: In which city did the mystic and poet Jalal al-Din Rumi work?
q-islamische-welt-35#explanation: Rumi lived and taught in Konya in Anatolia, where his tomb also lies. The order of the whirling dervishes emerged from his circle.
q-islamische-welt-36#question: What is Rabia of Basra known for?
q-islamische-welt-36#choices.0: As the wife of Caliph Harun al-Rashid
q-islamische-welt-36#choices.1: As founder of the al-Qarawiyyin mosque in Fez
q-islamische-welt-36#choices.2: As a sultana who ruled Egypt for a time
q-islamische-welt-36#choices.3: As an early Sufi mystic who taught pure love of God
q-islamische-welt-36#explanation: Rabia lived in Basra in the 8th century and taught that God should be served not out of fear or hope but out of love. She is considered one of the formative figures of Sufism.
q-islamische-welt-37#choices.1: Transmitted sayings and deeds of the Prophet
q-islamische-welt-37#choices.3: Legal opinions issued by a mufti
q-islamische-welt-37#explanation: In the 8th and 9th centuries scholars collected hadiths and tested their reliability. Alongside the Quran they became the most important basis of Islamic law; the chapters of the Quran, by contrast, are called suras.
q-islamische-welt-38#explanation: In a madrasa students learned mainly law, Quranic interpretation and grammar, often also mathematics and medicine. Many were funded by rulers or wealthy benefactors.
q-islamische-welt-39#question: Which mosque and centre of learning, still in existence today, did the Fatimids found in Cairo in 970?
q-islamische-welt-39#explanation: Al-Azhar has been a place of learning for over a thousand years and is today one of the most respected universities of the Sunni world. Al-Qarawiyyin is in Fez, the Mezquita in Córdoba.
q-islamische-welt-40#question: Who were the Mamluks who ruled Egypt from 1250?
q-islamische-welt-40#choices.1: Military slaves who rose to rule themselves
q-islamische-welt-40#choices.2: Persian nobles in the service of the Abbasids
q-islamische-welt-40#choices.3: A Berber tribe from the Atlas Mountains
q-islamische-welt-40#explanation: Mamluks were bought as young slaves, mostly from the steppes and the Caucasus, and trained as cavalry warriors. In Egypt they seized power and defeated the Mongols in 1260.
q-islamische-welt-41#question: Which woman ruled Egypt for a time as sultana in the 13th century?
q-islamische-welt-41#explanation: Shajar al-Durr led the defence against the crusade of Louis IX in 1249–50 and then briefly ruled as sultana. Radiyya, by contrast, reigned in the Delhi Sultanate.
q-islamische-welt-42#question: Through which victory did Saladin clear his way to Jerusalem in 1187?
q-islamische-welt-42#explanation: At Hattin in Galilee, Saladin destroyed the army of the crusader states. A few months later Jerusalem surrendered to him.
q-islamische-welt-43#question: Which of these events happened last?
q-islamische-welt-43#choices.1: Abd al-Rahman III proclaims the Caliphate of Córdoba
q-islamische-welt-43#explanation: The destruction of Baghdad by Hulagu in 1258 came after Saladin's recapture of Jerusalem in 1187, the victory at Manzikert in 1071 and the Caliphate of Córdoba in 929. It ended the Abbasid caliphate.
q-islamische-welt-44#question: Which country did the traveller Ibn Battuta come from?
q-islamische-welt-44#explanation: Ibn Battuta set out from Tangier on pilgrimage to Mecca in 1325 and only returned in 1349, after almost 25 years; he later travelled on to al-Andalus and Mali. His travel account describes lands from West Africa to China.
q-islamische-welt-45#question: Which dynasty built the Alhambra in Granada?
q-islamische-welt-45#explanation: The Nasrid sultans expanded the palace city mainly in the 14th century. Their last emir surrendered Granada to the Catholic Monarchs in 1492.
q-islamische-welt-46#question: Which city on the Niger became a symbol of Islamic learning in West Africa in the 14th century?
q-islamische-welt-46#explanation: Timbuktu had famous mosques and scholars, some of whose manuscripts survive to this day. Kilwa and Zanzibar, by contrast, lay on the East African coast.
q-islamische-welt-47#question: Which commodity did caravans mainly carry north across the Sahara from West Africa?
q-islamische-welt-47#explanation: West African gold was in great demand around the Mediterranean and made empires such as Mali wealthy. Silk and porcelain, by contrast, came from China and pepper from India.
q-islamische-welt-48#question: Which winds did Muslim sailors use for regular voyages across the Indian Ocean?
q-islamische-welt-48#explanation: The monsoon blows in opposite directions in summer and winter, so ships could sail from Arabia to India and back again. This made ports such as Basra and Aden rich.
q-islamische-welt-49#question: Which crop did Muslims spread in Spain?
q-islamische-welt-49#explanation: With new irrigation techniques, Muslims brought sugar cane, rice, cotton and citrus fruits to al-Andalus. Potatoes, maize and tobacco, by contrast, come from the Americas.
q-islamische-welt-50#question: What is the engineer al-Jazari known for?
q-islamische-welt-50#choices.0: Describing pumps, water clocks and automata
q-islamische-welt-50#choices.2: The most accurate star catalogue of his time
q-islamische-welt-50#explanation: Around 1200 al-Jazari described dozens of mechanical devices with precise construction instructions and drawings. His book is regarded as a high point of medieval engineering.
q-islamische-welt-51#question: Who wrote the Persian national epic Shahnameh, the Book of Kings?
q-islamische-welt-51#explanation: Ferdowsi completed the Shahnameh around 1010; it tells the history of Iran from mythical times to the Arab conquest. Hafez and Omar Khayyam, by contrast, became famous for lyric poems and quatrains.
q-islamische-welt-52#question: Why did Islamic artists bring calligraphy and ornament to the highest perfection?
q-islamische-welt-52#choices.0: Because figurative images were avoided in mosques
q-islamische-welt-52#choices.1: Because paper was too expensive for pictures
q-islamische-welt-52#choices.2: Because there were no stone sculptors
q-islamische-welt-52#choices.3: Because colours were forbidden in Islam
q-islamische-welt-52#explanation: As mosques did without images of humans and animals, they were decorated with Quranic verses in fine script, geometric patterns and arabesques. Coloured tiles and mosaics show that colour was certainly permitted.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-01#question: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-01#explanation: On November 9, 1989 the GDR opened the border crossings; reunification followed on October 3, 1990.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-02#question: Which crisis brought the world to the brink of nuclear war in 1962?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-02#explanation: Soviet missiles in Cuba led in October 1962 to a thirteen-day confrontation between Kennedy and Khrushchev.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-04#question: By what method did Mahatma Gandhi win independence for India?
